title: Single nucleotide polymorphism markers for low‐dose aspirin‐associated peptic ulcer and ulcer bleeding

sections.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:sec><jats:title>Background and Aim</jats:title><jats:p>In our previous study, the <jats:italic><jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SLCO</jats:styled-content>1<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">B</jats:styled-content>1</jats:italic> 521<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">TT</jats:styled-content> genotype and the <jats:italic><jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SLCO</jats:styled-content>1<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">B</jats:styled-content>1</jats:italic>*1b haplotype were significantly associated with the risk of peptic ulcer in patients taking low‐dose aspirin (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">LDA</jats:styled-content>). The aim of the present study was to investigate pharmacogenomic profile of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">LDA</jats:styled-content>‐induced peptic ulcer and ulcer bleeding.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Methods</jats:title><jats:p>Patients taking 100 mg of enteric‐coated aspirin for cardiovascular diseases and with a peptic ulcer or ulcer bleeding and patients who also participated in endoscopic surveillance were studied. Genome‐wide analysis of single nucleotide polymorphisms (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNPs</jats:styled-content>) was performed using the <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">A</jats:styled-content>ffymetrix <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">DME P</jats:styled-content>lus <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">P</jats:styled-content>remier <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">P</jats:styled-content>ack. <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">S<jats:italic>LCO</jats:italic></jats:styled-content><jats:italic>1<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">B</jats:styled-content>1</jats:italic>*1b haplotype and candidate genotypes of genes associated with ulcer bleeding or small bowel bleeding identified by genome‐wide analysis were determined using <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">T</jats:styled-content>aq<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">M</jats:styled-content>an <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SNP G</jats:styled-content>enotyping <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">A</jats:styled-content>ssay kits, polymerase chain reaction‐restriction fragment length polymorphism, and direct sequencing.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Results</jats:title><jats:p>Of 593 patients enrolled, 111 patients had a peptic ulcer and 45 had ulcer bleeding. The frequencies of the <jats:italic><jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SLCO</jats:styled-content>1<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">B</jats:styled-content>1</jats:italic>*1b haplotype and <jats:italic><jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CHST</jats:styled-content>2</jats:italic> 2082 <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">T</jats:styled-content> allele were significantly greater in patients with peptic ulcer and ulcer bleeding compared to the controls. After adjustment for significant factors, the <jats:italic><jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SLCO</jats:styled-content>1<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">B</jats:styled-content>1</jats:italic>*1b haplotype was associated with peptic ulcer (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">OR</jats:styled-content> 2.20, 95% <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CI</jats:styled-content> 1.24–3.89) and <jats:italic><jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CHST</jats:styled-content>2</jats:italic> 2082 <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">T</jats:styled-content> allele with ulcer bleeding (2.57, 1.07–6.17).</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title><jats:p>The <jats:italic><jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">CHST</jats:styled-content>2</jats:italic> 2082 <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">T</jats:styled-content> allele as well as <jats:italic><jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">SLCO</jats:styled-content>1<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">B</jats:styled-content>1*1b</jats:italic> haplotype may identify patients at increa
